_comment: The demo, as data. It used to be a heredoc inside capture-demo-video.sh,
which meant the CONTENT of the demo — the thing a viewer actually judges —
was not reviewable in a pull request. It is now.
Every claim the run makes must already be in docs/launch-copy.md's
'Reference facts' block. The app renders its own decode rate in the footer,
so the numbers on screen are measured live rather than asserted by a
caption: nothing here needs to state a figure.
The opening turn does NOT ask the model where it runs. It used to ask
'what are you running on, and where does the model live?', and lfm25-350m
answered 'The model resides in the cloud at AWS, and it's hosted globally
to ensure low-latency access' — in a frame whose own watermark reads
'local · no cloud'. A 350M model has no way to know where it is deployed,
so the question invites a confabulation, and it would have been the first
thing a README visitor read. The local-and-offline claim is made by the
watermark, the UI and the README, all of which can be checked; asking the
model to attest to it is neither evidence nor a demo of anything.
Shows what the product is TODAY. The v1.2.0 demo was Phase 6 — one 350M
chat and one image — and predates the coding tier, the thinking tier with
the CoT cut, KV reuse across a conversation switch, and the LAN API.
Coding tier is shown with qwen25-coder-1.5b, not the 3B. Same tier, and
the choice is pacing rather than flattery: the 3B decodes at 14 tok/s
against 26, which on a 90-second video means one answer eats the demo.
The footer shows the live rate either way, so nothing here is hidden.
n_predict is 400, not the 120 this script used first. At 120 the coding
turn hit the cap (log: n=120) and the capture ended on '// Function to
reverse a linked list in' — a truncated comment, with the requested
function never written, under a status line reading 'Done'. The prompt
also asks for the function alone: unprompted, the model spent its budget
on includes, a struct and a newNode helper before reaching the answer.
Bounding the question is how a demo fits on screen; capping the answer
mid-sentence is how it shows a failure and calls it a feature.
NO thinking turn, and the reason is measured rather than editorial.
lfm25-1.2b-thinking was in this script and produced no answer: at
n_predict 120 it spent the whole budget reasoning, and raising it to 768
changed nothing — the console log shows 'reply 768' and 'n=768' followed
by 'postprocess left no answer (truncated reasoning block)', i.e. it burned
every token without closing <think>, on 'a train leaves at 14:05 and takes
3h40'. That cost 24 of 66 seconds to display the stand-in message. The app
is behaving correctly — keeping the turn instead of losing it is what the
thinkcut gate pins — but a showcase must show a result. The tier stays in
the product and the catalogue; what is measured about it is tracked
separately, since nothing in the repo yet proves a reasoning turn ever
completes (it is absent from the H9 suite).
No 'quit': the capture keeps running for a few frames after the last
action, and an app that exited would hand them Dev Home.
show_pane opens a ContentDialog, holds it for the capture, and closes it in
the same action — see uwp/MainPage.cpp. A pane left open would sit over
everything that follows.

actions.text: In two sentences: why would someone run a language model on their own hardware?
Write a C function that reverses a singly linked list in place. Just the function, no main and no explanation.
